Body details, preferences and daily goals

VitQuest works offline. Everything you record (profile, goals, steps, food, weight, water, workouts, habits and reminders) is stored only on this device. The only exception is a food photo you choose to send for an AI estimate: it goes to VitQuest’s server and Google Gemini, and is not stored there. If you connect Health Connect, VitQuest only reads daily step totals. App data is excluded from cloud backups; export a backup to keep your own copy.
Remove all your records and settings from this device

Everything you recorded (profile, goals, steps, food diary and food photos, meal plans, weight, water, workouts, habits and reminders) and your settings will be permanently removed from this device. Backup files you exported and data in Health Connect are not affected. This cannot be undone.
Save all your records and settings to a file you choose, then restore them on this phone or a new one. The file is not encrypted and contains your health data, so keep it somewhere private.
Saves a JSON file. Nothing is uploaded by VitQuest.

Steps from different sources are never added together. One source is chosen for each day, and a manual entry always replaces automatic data for that day.

On HyperOS and MIUI, allow Autostart and set Battery to “No restrictions” for VitQuest, or the system may stop counting. This uses more battery than counting only while the app is open.
See what the phone sensors report
Raw numbers behind your step count, so a wrong count can be traced. They are shown here only and never leave the phone.
The raw value is the phone’s own total since it was last restarted. If it barely rises while you walk, the phone’s counter is missing steps and the motion count is the better source.
Keeps counting with the screen off
Counted from the accelerometer, after about 8 steps in a row so that picking the phone up does not count. Readings that stop rising while you walk mean the system paused VitQuest.
Shown while VitQuest counts steps in the background
Food photo estimates are not set up in this build. They need VitQuest’s server settings (see docs/AI_SETUP.md). Everything else works without them.

The photo is sent over the internet to VitQuest’s server, which asks Google Gemini to recognise the food and estimate portions and calories. The server does not keep the photo. On Gemini’s free tier, Google may use what is sent to improve its products, so only photograph food, not people or documents. A small copy stays on this phone so you can see the meal again.
Take or choose a photo of your meal or drink. You can check and change every item before it is saved.
Tips: photograph from above, in good light, with the whole plate visible. Sauces, oil and sugar in drinks are hard to see, so check those.

Enter a name, a weight from 1 to 3000 g and energy from 0 to 5000 kcal.

The phone’s step counter starts when you enable it, and steps before a restart that were not yet read can be lost. VitQuest’s motion count only sees steps while the app is open or background counting is on. Health Connect shows only data that your phone or other apps write to it.
A manual entry replaces automatic data for this day. Remove it to go back to automatic data.
Increase your goal gradually as walking becomes easier.

VitQuest will only read your daily step count from Health Connect to show your progress. It does not write anything and the data stays on this device. You can remove access at any time in Health Connect.
Android will ask for the Physical activity permission so VitQuest can read your phone\'s step counter. Steps are stored only on this device. You can turn this off at any time in system settings.

VitQuest reads only your daily step totals from Health Connect. They are used to show today\'s steps, your weekly progress and your step history. VitQuest does not write to Health Connect, does not read any other health data, and does not send health data to any server or third party. Data stays on this device and is deleted when you use Delete all data in Settings or uninstall the app. You can withdraw access at any time in Health Connect.

Why a reminder may be late

Android and battery savers (such as on HyperOS) can delay or block background work, so times are approximate, not exact. If reminders do not appear, allow VitQuest to run without battery restrictions and check that its notifications are on.
